summary: Siuslaw NF lookout: 1942 platform and cabin, a 40-ft steel tower in 1958, staffed into 1972, dismantled 1973; now gone, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 7 x 7 steel cab on the 1958 40-foot tower, per the Oregon list
facts.status_note: Dismantled at the end of the 1973 season, per the Oregon list. The register and firelookout.com also list it as gone.

staffing.status: last staffed season 1972, per the Oregon list

events.note: 10-foot platform and AWS cabin, per the register and firelookout.com.
Oliver Cowan in charge of the lookout (Coos Bay Times, February 1943, quoted on the Oregon list).
Activation date October 5, 1943. The Oregon list names the Eugene Filter Center beside it and does not explain.
Coos Bay Times reports William Sylvester relieved of summer work; lookout closed October 1.
40-foot steel tower with 7 x 7 steel cab erected by a forest crew, replacing the 1942 platform and cabin.
Used for emergency in the 1970s, per the register.
Final season the lookout was staffed.
Used as an emergency station and dismantled at the end of the season.
Registered February 10, 2011, on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com describe a 10-foot platform with an AWS cabin, dated 1942. The Oregon list describes a roughly 12-foot round timber tower with an open platform and gives no date. The story reports both.
The 12.2 m (40 ft) height in the brief matches the 1958 tower. The Oregon list's 12-foot first structure is a different structure and is not used for height.

notes_for_editor: Gone lookout. The newspaper items are quoted on the Oregon list, not checked against the Coos Bay Times itself. The register and the Oregon list disagree on the first structure (10-foot platform versus roughly 12-foot timber tower), and the story reports both. The Eugene Filter Center activation is unexplained, so the story reports it without interpreting. No source states current access, so no access level is set. PeakVisor gives 349 m elevation against the register's 357 m; the register figure is used. The road note comes only from PeakVisor, a summit database.
